findings.title: Duplicate arguments bypass the graph and node binding proof
findings.criterion_ref: PKGV2-T10 — the suite must positively prove PKGV2-T01 through PKGV2-T09; PKGV2-T01 requires the package graph binding to be structurally enforced, and PKGV2-T05 requires each scan to use its exact node ID.
findings.trigger: A scan command retains the expected `--graph` or `--node` pair but appends a second pair with the parent graph or another node ID.
findings.consequence: Python argparse uses the last occurrence, so execution scans the wrong graph or node. The validator and automated suite inspect only the first occurrence and still pass, allowing the same stale-write-set false assurance the package is intended to make structurally impossible.
findings.evidence: `validate_plan_v2.py` lines 241–259 checks membership and obtains values with `command.index(...)`, but never requires either flag to occur exactly once. Tests at lines 288–310 use the same first-occurrence logic. Direct mutations showed `duplicate_node_accepted True` and `duplicate_graph_accepted True`; argparse resolved `--node N20 ... --node N30` and `--graph package ... --graph parent` to N30 and the parent graph.

observations: Round 1’s exact defects are repaired: simple wrong-node and wrong-graph substitutions and parent-root result/evidence writes are now rejected, with corresponding mutation tests.
The current graph contains no duplicate flags; N20–N50 use their exact IDs and the package-v2 graph, while N60 alone uses complete-tree mode.

The three prompts still name the deprecated package-local `implementation.graph.v1.yaml`; N00 requires it to exist, and N20/N30 show commands using it, although the active artifact is `implementation.graph.v2.yaml`. The numbered criteria constrain the graph commands and prompt ownership language rather than these prompt command examples, so this is recorded as a non-blocking observation.

In the read-only environment, 34 tests not requiring temporary-file creation passed and all 36 tests collected. The two synthetic-tree tests could not be executed here because pytest's `tmp_path` requires writable storage; their unchanged logic was inspected directly.
reasoning: Historical hashes, source-spec binding, ownership, write-set uniqueness, scan narrowing, result roots, and production-path git status were checked and remain correct. The prior finding’s stated mutations are now covered. A separate major T10 proof gap survives because duplicate argparse options let a wrong runtime binding pass both newly added enforcement layers.
